1315.01 DEFINITIONS.
   As used in this chapter:
   (a)   “Building Code” means those provisions of the Building Code officially
adopted by the City of Elyria, or other such codes officially designated by the
City of Elyria, for the regulation of construction, alteration, addition,
repair, location, occupancy and maintenance of buildings and structures.
   (b)   “Chief Building Official” means the official who is charged with the
administration and enforcement of the Building Code, or any duly authorized
representative.
   (c)   “Person” means an individual, corporation, partnership or any other
group acting as a unit.
   (d)   “Registered design professional” means an architect or engineer who is
registered or licensed to practice professional architecture or engineering in
the State of Ohio.
(Ord. 95-289. Passed 12-18-95; Ord. 2013-69. Passed 6-3-13.)
1315.02 ESTABLISHMENT; APPOINTMENT OF MEMBERS.
   There is hereby established a Board of Building Standards and Appeals,
consisting of not less than five nor more than seven members, appointed by the
Mayor as follows: one for five years; one for four years; one for three years;
one for two years; and one for one year. Thereafter, each new member shall
serve for five years or until a successor has been appointed. Alternate members
shall serve at the pleasure of the Mayor for terms of not more than five years.
(Ord. 95-289. Passed 12-18-95; Ord. 2013-69. Passed 6-3-13.)
1315.03 QUALIFICATIONS OF MEMBERS; PERSONAL INTEREST.
   (a)   The Board of Building Standards and Appeals shall consist of not less
than five individuals, one from each of the following professional disciplines:
      (1)   A registered design professional, to wit: a registered architect,
or a builder or superintendent of building construction with at least five
years experience.
      (2)   A registered design professional with structural engineering or
architectural experience.
      (3)   A registered design professional with mechanical or plumbing
engineering experience or a mechanical or plumbing contractor with at least
five years of experience.
      (4)   A registered design professional with electrical engineering
experience or an electrical contractor with at least five years experience.
      (5)   A registered design professional with fire protection engineering
experience or a fire protection contractor with at least five years of
experience.
   (b)   Contractor appointees shall be registered in the Building Department.
   (c)   A member of Council, the City Engineer, the Chief Building Official,
the Fire Chief or his or her designee, of the City, and the County Health
Commissioner shall be members ex officio.
   (d)   No member shall participate in any proceeding in which that member has
any personal, professional or financial interest.
(Ord. 95-289. Passed 12-18-95; Ord. 2013-69. Passed 6-3-13; Ord. 2017-5. Passed
2-6-17.)
1315.04 ALTERNATE MEMBERS.
   The Mayor shall appoint two alternate members who shall be called by the
Board Chairperson to hear appeals during the absence or recusal of a member.
Alternate members shall meet the qualifications set forth under Section
1315.03.
(Ord. 95-289. Passed 12-18-95; Ord. 2013-69. Passed 6-3-13.)
1315.05 OFFICERS; MEETINGS; RULES AND REGULATIONS.
   (a)   The Board of Building Standards and Appeals shall annually select one
of its members, including alternate members, to serve as Chairperson.
   (b)   The Mayor shall designate a person to serve as Secretary to the Board.
The Secretary shall file a detailed record of all proceedings in the Building
Department. The Secretary must record the vote of each member upon every
question or indicate reasons for failure to vote.
   (c)   The Board of Building Standards and Appeals shall meet upon notice
from the Chairperson or at scheduled periodic meetings. All meetings shall be
open to the public.
   (d)   A majority of the members shall constitute a quorum. One less than a
majority of members may adjourn a meeting when a quorum is not present.
   (e)   The Board of Building Standards shall adopt, and make available to the
public through its Secretary, its own rules and regulations and procedures
under which a hearing will be conducted. The procedures shall not require
compliance with strict rules of evidence, but shall mandate that only relevant
information be presented.
(Ord. 95-289. Passed 12-18-95; Ord. 2013-69. Passed 6-3-13.)
1315.06 POWERS AND DUTIES.
   (a)   The Board of Building Standards and Appeals shall determine the
suitability of materials and types of construction and methods of installation,
and shall provide for reasonable interpretations of the provisions of the
Building Code, relevant to same.
   (b)   The Board shall hear appeals of persons aggrieved by the provisions of
the Building Code or by decisions of the Chief Building Official, with the
exception of proceedings pursuant to the provisions of
Chapter 1391 of these Codified Ordinances, which exclusively govern
condemnation and demolition proceedings.
   (c)   The Board shall aid the Chief Building Official, when requested, in
the enforcement of the Building Code, as defined herein.
   (d)   The Board shall have the power to accept or reject plans when the same
are presented for review by the Chief Building Official in accordance with this
chapter.
   (e)   The Board shall provide for the current updating of the Building Code
and may advise Council of the necessity for amending provisions of the Code.
   (f)   The Board shall vary the application of any provision of the Building
Code, as defined in this chapter, to any particular case when, in its opinion,
enforcement thereof would do manifest injustice or would be contrary to the
spirit and purpose of the Code or the public interest.
   (g)   The Board shall determine any requirement for the strength or
stability of any existing building or structure, or for the safety or health of
the occupants thereof, not specifically covered by the Building Code or
Chapter 1391 of the Elyria Codified Ordinances, or not readily interpretable
from the provisions of the Code or Codified Ordinances.
   (h)   Nothing in this chapter shall be construed, for purposes of an appeal
of a condemnation or demolition order pursuant to
Chapter 1391 of the Elyria Codified Ordinances, as a conferral of jurisdiction
upon the Board of Building Standards of Appeals.
(Ord. 95-289. Passed 12-18-95; Ord. 2013-69. Passed 6-3-13.)
1315.07 APPEALS PROCEDURE.
   (a)   Any person affected by a decision of the Chief Building Official or a
notice or order issued under the Building Code, other than an order of
condemnation and/or demolition pursuant to Chapter 1391 of the Elyria Codified
Ordinances, shall have the right to appeal to the Board of Building Standards
and Appeals, provided that a written application for appeal is filed within
twenty days after the day that the decision, notice or order was served. An
application for appeal shall be based on a claim that the true intent of the
Building Code, as defined herein, or the rules legally adopted thereunder have
been incorrectly interpreted, or that the provisions of the Code do not fully
apply or that the requirements of the Code are adequately satisfied by other
means.
   (b)   The Board shall hold a hearing within the period of time prescribed
and render a decision within a reasonable time which shall not exceed ten days
from the hearing of the appeal. The Board may affirm, reject, revoke, institute
suspension, recommend prosecution or decide an appeal in the best interest of
the appellant or the City, or both.
   (c)   The decision of the Board shall be by resolution. Copies shall be
furnished to the appellant and to the Chief Building Official.
   (d)   All hearings shall be given public notice in a manner determined by
the Board. The appellant, the appellant's representative, the Chief Building
Official and any person whose interests are affected shall be given an
opportunity to be heard.
   (e)   Majority vote shall rule, except that the Board shall modify or
reverse the decision of the Chief Building Official only by a concurring vote
of three members.
   (f)   When five members are not present to hear an appeal, the appellant
shall have the right to request a postponement of the hearing.
   (g)   The Chief Building Official shall take immediate action in accordance
with the decision of the Board.
(Ord. 95-289. Passed 12-18-95; Ord. 2013-69. Passed 6-3-13.)
1315.08 JUDICIAL REVIEW.
   A person shall have the right to appeal the final order of the Board of
Building Standards and Appeals to a court of competent jurisdiction, pursuant
to Ohio R.C. Chapter 2505. The right to appeal provided by Ohio R.C. 2506.01 is
in addition to any other remedy of appeal provided by law.
(Ord. 95-289. Passed 12-18-95; Ord. 2013-69. Passed 6-3-13.)

1317.06 DEFINITION OF REPAIRS.
   As used in this chapter, "repairs" means the replacement of existing
material with the same kind of material, but not including work that would
affect the structural safety of a building or that would affect or change
required existing facilities or that would affect a vital element of an
elevator, plumbing or gas piping, wiring or heating installation, or a
provision of law or ordinance.
(Ord. 4693. Passed 6-4-56.)
1317.07 PENALTY FEE.
   If any work for which a permit is required by law is commenced without such
a permit by any person who had knowledge, or should have had knowledge, that
the work required a permit, then the fees required by the permit shall be
doubled, but the payment of such double fee shall not relieve any person from
fully complying with the requirements or regulations governing building,
plumbing, wiring, heating and cooling in the City.
(Ord. 97-275. Passed 11-3-97.)
1317.08 CERTIFICATE OF OCCUPANCY.
   Whenever there is a change in the use or occupancy of a building or other
structure or premises, or part thereof, which new use or occupancy results in
reclassification of the building or other structure or premises, or part
thereof, under a different occupancy or use classification of this Building
Code, such building or other structure or premises shall not be used or
occupied until a Certificate of Occupancy therefor has been issued by the
Building Inspector. Whenever a building or other structure for which a
Certificate of Occupancy had not been previously issued is enlarged or altered,
the use or occupancy of such building or other structure, if not discontinued
while work was done, shall not be continued for more than thirty days after the
completion of the work, and if vacated while work was done, such building or
other structure shall not be used or occupied, until a Certificate of Occupancy
has been issued by the Inspector. Application for a Certificate of Occupancy
shall be made by the owner or his or her authorized representative on forms
obtained from the Inspector.
(Ord. 97-5. Passed 1-6-97.)
1317.09 CERTIFICATE OF APPROVAL.
   (a)   Certificate Required; Contents. A Certificate of Approval shall be
required. The Certificate shall state the following: the nature of the
occupancy authorized; that the building was erected in compliance with the
approved plans and provisions governing building, plumbing, wiring, heating and
cooling in the City; the intended use of the building or premises as stated by
the applicant, in terms of the wording of the Planning and Zoning Code; the
number of families proposed to be housed; if the building is a dwelling house
or apartment house; the zoning district in which the property is located; that
the building and the proposed use are in compliance with the Planning and
Zoning Code; and that all work requiring inspection is approved by the Building
Department.
   (b)   Sidewalks. No Certificate of Approval shall be issued for a building
on any sublot, except if:
      (1)   A one-course Portland cement concrete sidewalk, four feet in width,
has been constructed along all lot frontages, and such construction has been
approved by the City Engineer; or
      (2)   A cash bond or irrevocable letter of credit has been posted with
the City Auditor in an amount approved by the City Engineer; or
      (3)   The owners of record have signed and delivered to the City Engineer
an affidavit stating that said owners have a valid contract for the
construction of sidewalks on all frontages of the real property and that the
funds for the construction of said sidewalks are being held by a designated
escrow agent, that the owners and their heirs, successors and assigns waived
any and all claims against the City for the failure of said sidewalks being
constructed and that the owners and their heirs, successors and assigns waive
any and all notice requirements for future assessments by the City for sidewalk
construction if said sidewalks have not been constructed to meet City standards
within six months from the date of issuance of the Certificate of Approval.
(Ord. 97-5. Passed 1-6-97; Ord. 2007-52. Passed 5-7-07.)
1317.10 TIME LIMITS OF BUILDING PERMITS.
   (a)   A permit issued by the Building Department shall expire twelve months
after its issuance if no substantial work is commenced upon the site of the
project for which the permit was issued.
   (b)   One extension shall be granted for an additional twelve-month period
if requested by the owner at least ten days in advance of the expiration of the
permit and upon payment of a fee of not more than one hundred dollars
($100.00).
   (c)   If, in the course of construction, work is delayed or suspended for
more than six months, the approval of plans, drawings, specifications or data
is invalid. Two extensions shall be granted for six months each if requested by
the owner at least ten days in advance of the expiration of the permit and upon
payment of a fee, for each extension, of not more than one hundred dollars
($100.00).
(Ord. 86-228. Passed 11-17-86.)

1317.12 FEE WAIVER.
   Any and all permit fees are hereby waived for any renovation to City
facilities for purposes of compliance with the Americans With Disabilities Act
(ADA).

1319.03 HYDRANTS AND WATER MAINS.
   The City Engineer, Building Inspector, Superintendent of the Bureau of Water
Distribution and the Arson and Fire Prevention Bureau are hereby authorized to
inform all parties applying for building permits for new construction,
additions to present buildings or additional new construction of the following:
All commercial and industrial establishments, mercantile, educational and
institutional occupancy, places of assembly, hotels, motels, multi-family
dwellings, dwelling groups (i.e.: apartments, condominium. and cluster
developments), mobile trailer home sites and trailer sites shall show on their
construction plans placement of hydrants and size of water mains according to
the following specifications:
   (a)   A minimum of two hydrants within 500 feet of any building, mobile home
or trailer;
   (b)   No part of a building shall be more than 300 feet from a hydrant;
   (c)   Hydrants, including the installation, construction and repair and
maintenance thereof shall meet City specifications and standards, and all
applicable laws and regulations;
   (d)   Size of mains, as follows:
      (1)   Minimum size shall be eight inches;
      (2)   Main structure shall be grid connected if possible; grid connector
minimum shall be six inches;
      (3)   The location of fire hydrants on both public and private property
shall be approved by the Fire Chief before a building permit is issued;
   (e)   All hydrants and water mains installed, constructed, or maintained on
private real property within the City shall have legal rights-of-way (e.g.
easements to the City) and procedures as approved by the City necessary for the
proper maintenance, repair and control thereof. The City shall have the right
to enter upon any real property containing private hydrants and water mains
whenever the Safety-Service Director, in his or her sole discretion, determines
that it is necessary for the health, safety and welfare of the public to
maintain or repair any hydrant or water main on private property. The cost of
any such maintenance or repair shall be done at the expense of the owner of the
real property.
   (f)   Driveway arrangement shall be designed so that fire equipment can
reach hydrants at all times by the use of such drives.
   (g)   The centerline of hydrants shall be located not less than two feet,
six inches and not more than six feet from the back of the street curb or from
the paved surface of the driveway or parking area Such distance may be exceeded
only if the Safety-Service Director finds the locations to be impractical.
   (h)   Unless exempted by the Director, mobile home parks and building
complexes under one ownership, which require six or more fire hydrants, shall
be on a looped system with two connection points to City water mains.
   (i)   When an existing fire hydrant is located within 1,000 feet of the
farthest point of a proposed new structure, as measured along the usable path
for laying a fire hose, a building permit for a nonresidential structure may be
issued after Council has authorized a contract for the construction of a water
main, or a developer has posted a bond with the City covering the construction
of a proposed water main, or if the site plan of the proposed new structure
includes a water main extension and fire hydrants at locations meeting the
requirements of subsections (a) and (b) hereof. No building shall be utilized
or otherwise occupied until the hydrants required by subsections (a) and (b)
hereof are in service.
   The distances specified in subsections (a) and (b) hereof shall be measured
along the routes of travel of fire apparatus, or along the route that the fire
hose would be laid as appropriately determined by the Fire Chief or his or her
representative.
(Ord. 84-97. Passed 4-16-84; Ord. 2004-50. Passed 4-5-04.)

1321.01 REGISTRATION REQUIRED FOR CERTAIN PERSONS.
   The persons, firms or corporations enumerated in Section
1321.02 shall be required to register with the Building Department, and to pay
an annual registration fee as required in Section
1321.04.
(Ord. 62-180. Passed 12-3-62.)
1321.02 DEFINITIONS.
   As used in this chapter:
   (a)   "General building contractor I" means a person, firm or corporation
who or which contracts for the erection, remodeling, alteration, addition to
and repair of buildings or structures governed by this Part Thirteen - Building
Code, including the standards adopted in this Part Thirteen - Building Code by
reference.
   (b)   "Building contractor II" means a person, firm or corporation who or
which contracts for the erection, remodeling, alteration, addition to and
repair of buildings governed by the Dwelling House Code and any and all laws
governing one, two and/or three-family dwellings, also provisions of this Part
Thirteen - Building Code.
   (c)   "Building contractor III" means a person, firm or corporation who or
which engages in masonry and concrete work (brick and block laying, driveways,
sidewalks, footers, concrete foundations); remodeling, additions, alterations
and repair of one, two and/or three-family dwellings and accessory buildings;
or siding applicators engaged in residing of buildings.
   (d)   "Excavating and trenching contractor" means a person, firm or
corporation who or which contracts to dig excavations for basements, footer
trenches, trenching for and laying of sewer piping to buildings or structures
from point of connection in the public right of way, trenching for utility
lines to building or structure. This registration shall be confirmed by the
City Engineer.
   (e)   "Master plumbing contractor" means a person, firm or corporation who
or which contracts to engage in the installation, repair or replacement of
sanitary fixtures; piping necessary for disposal of wastes; piping for water
lines and gas lines; installation, replacement or repair of hot water heaters;
installation, replacement or repair of hot water and/or steam heating systems;
and installation, repair, replacement or testing of backflow prevention
devices.
   (f)   "Electrical contractor" means a person, firm or corporation who or
which contracts to engage in the installation, repair or replacement of
electric wiring and wiring for electric heating, fixtures, equipment or devices
governed by the Ohio Basic Building Code, the Dwelling House Code and the
provisions of Chapter
1361 of this Part Thirteen - Building Code. When an installation of air
conditioning units entails duct work and/or the changing of a unit, such phase
shall be performed by registered heating and refrigeration contractors.
   (g)   "Electrical Contractor II" means a person, firm or corporation who or
which contracts to engage in the installation, repair or replacement of
electrical signs, fire protection equipment or devices, mobile home hook-ups
only, ground fault interrupters for swimming pools, alarm monitoring and cable
systems.
   (h)   "Sign erector" means a person, firm or corporation who or which
contracts to erect, replace or repair signs advertising the occupancy or
business within or on the premises for which a sign is provided. Electrical
wiring for signs from fuse panel to sign outlet, shall be performed by a
registered electrical contractor.
   (i)   "Outdoor signboard, billboard erector" means a person, firm or
corporation who or which contracts to erect, replace or repair signs
advertising other than the use or occupancy of the premises on which they are
erected. Electrical work for this category shall be performed by a registered
electrical contractor.
   (j)   "Heating contractor" means a person, firm or corporation who or which,
pursuant to the Heating and Cooling Code (Ordinance 62-163, passed December 3,
1962) performs installation of gas lines, prefabricated chimneys, cleaning of
furnaces, installation of gutters and downspouts and roofing work.
   (k)   "Contractor in demolishing and/or moving of buildings" means a person,
firm or corporation who or which contracts to demolish or move buildings.
   (l)   "Roofer, tinsmith, gutter and downspout contractor" means a person,
firm or corporation who or which contracts to install, replace or repair
gutters and/or downspouts and work pertinent thereto, and application of
roofing materials.
   (m)   "Lawn irrigation contractor" means a person, firm or corporation who
or which contracts to construct, install, repair, wire, maintain or modify any
system that connects to the City water system to provide potable water for non-
potable uses such as lawns, flowerbeds, shrubs, trees, ornamental ponds,
fountains, waterfalls or other similar uses.
(Ord. 62-63. Passed 6-18-62; Ord. 79-200. Passed 8-20-79; Ord. 80-231. Passed
12-15-80; Ord. 91-241. Passed 12-16-91; Ord. 2003-115. Passed 7-7-03.)
1321.03 REGISTRATION APPLICATION; RENEWAL.
   (a)   Application for registration shall be made to the Building Department
on forms provided therefor.
   (b)   Qualifications for registration are as follows:
      (1)   The applicant shall be at least twenty-one years of age;
      (2)   The applicant shall have had a minimum of five years of practical
experience; an affidavit to this effect shall be provided, except that a sewer
layer need have only three years of practical experience; in lieu of experience
required, the applicant may qualify with two years of technical training in an
accredited school, plus two years of practical experience, or hold a degree
from an accredited college or university in the business or trade in which he
applies to be registered;
      (3)   The applicant shall provide any and all references and in the
manner provided as may be requested on the application form;
      (4)   Each applicant shall provide proof of a twenty-five thousand dollar
($25,000) bond to be effective during the period of registration and the
applicant shall provide proof of a twenty-five thousand dollar ($25,000) bond
for any renewals.
(Ord. 87-311. Passed 12-7-87; Ord. 2017-29. Passed 3-20-17.)
      (5)   All registrations shall expire on December 31 of the year in which
they are in force. Renewal of registration may be commenced thirty days prior
to the expiration date. For renewal of registration, the final date will be
January 31 within the year that the registration is to be renewed.
(Ord. 2000-238. Passed 11-20-00.)
1321.04 INITIAL AND ANNUAL RENEWAL FEES.
   Upon approval of the application for registration and before a certificate
is issued, the contractor shall pay either an initial fee or an annual renewal
fee to the Building Department, as determined by Chapter
109 of the Administrative Code.
(Ord. 2000-238. Passed 11-20-00.)
1321.05 REVOCATION OF REGISTRATION.
   Registration may be revoked or suspended by the Building Inspector for any
of the following reasons:
   (a)   Violation of any of the provisions of this chapter or of this Building
Code;
   (b)   Misrepresentation of a material fact in order to become registered or
in the renewal of registration;
   (c)   Failure to secure permits, inspections and approvals required by this
Building Code and regulations of the Building Department;
   (d)   Use of registration to obtain a permit for another;
   (e)   Failure or refusal to correct a violation of the Building Code within
a prescribed period of time or to correct incompetent work as ordered by the
Building Inspector;
   (f)   Unethical business practices; a conviction involving moral turpitude;
or when revocation is deemed necessary in the public interest;
   (g)   For any valid reason adversely affecting the health, safety and
welfare of the residents of the City.
(Ord. 62-13. Passed 3-19-62.)
1321.06 WRITTEN NOTICE OF REVOCATION.
   (a)   The Building Inspector shall notify in writing persons affected and a
hearing shall be held by the Building Inspector on the revocation of a
registration.
   (b)   After proper hearing, the Building Inspector may revoke or suspend
registration for a period of not more than six months.
   (c)   Persons, firms or corporations aggrieved by the decision of the
Building Inspector may appeal within five days to the Board of Building
Standards and Appeals.
   (d)   A hearing shall be had by the Board of Building Standards and Appeals
and the Building Inspector's decision affirmed or rejected; if affirmed,
additional penalties may be prescribed by the Board.
(Ord. 62-13. Passed 3-19-62.)
1321.07 PERSONS EXEMPT FROM REGISTRATION.
   (a)   Single-Family Owner-Occupants. No provision of this chapter, or any
regulation adopted by authority of this chapter, shall be interpreted to
require that the owner of a single - or one-family dwelling shall be licensed
or registered personally to perform work upon the premises occupied, or to be
occupied, by the owner thereof as such owner's established residence. No such
person may build more than one new dwelling within a twenty-four month period
without obtaining property registration. Any such owner-occupant shall be
required to obtain necessary permits and perform work in accordance with this
Part Thirteen - Building Code. Such work shall be inspected. An oral test to
ascertain the abilities of the owner-occupant to perform work for which a
permit is required may be given by the Building Inspector. If, in the opinion
of the Inspector, during the oral test or during an inspection, it is
discovered that the ability of the owner-occupant is questionable, it may be
required that a registered contractor perform the work.
   (b)   Two- or Three-Family Owner-Occupants.
      (1)   No provision of this chapter, or any regulation adopted by
authority of this chapter, shall be interpreted to require that the owner of
any one-, two- or three-family dwelling shall be licensed or registered to
perform repairs, maintenance or alterations to such dwelling if such repairs,
maintenance or alterations do not affect the safety of any of the occupants of
such dwellings. Porch repair, roof covering replacement, window replacement,
siding installation, gutter installation and other non-structural items may be
done by the owner. However, any electrical, HVAC, plumbing and structural
repairs, maintenance or alterations shall require registered contractors.
      (2)   Further, no provision of this chapter or any regulation adopted by
authority of this chapter shall be interpreted to require that the owner of any
one-, two-, or three- family dwelling shall be licensed or registered to
construct or alter any building accessory to such one-, two-, or three-family
dwelling. Said owner shall be permitted to perform electrical and mechanical
installations and repairs to such accessory building.
      (3)   Construction plans and permits shall continue to be required.
   (c)   Government Agencies; Public Utilities. Provisions of registration
shall not apply to Federal, State, County or Municipal governmental agencies or
public utilities furnishing services to the City under Municipal-utilities
franchise agreements, nor to industrial, commercial or institutional
organizations wherein a maintenance department doing work within the provisions
of this Building Code is provided, except that should work covered by the
Building Code be contracted to outside concerns, then such contractors shall be
registered in the City as provided in this chapter.
(Ord. 91-105. Passed 6-3-91; Ord. 2002-13. Passed 1-22-02.)

1331.09 APPROVAL OF MATERIALS, DEVICES, ETC.
   All plumbing materials, devices, fixtures, appliances, and other equipment
used or installed in the City shall be of a type approved by the Board of
Building Standards. Unless specifically disapproved by formal action of the
Board, materials, devices, fixtures, appliances, and other equipment that bear
the label of approval of Underwriters' Laboratories, Inc., or any other agency
approved by the State Board of Building Standards, shall be deemed approved by
the Board.
(Ord. 2004-115. Passed 8-2-04.)

   The penalty for any violation of the provisions of Chapter
1331 shall be as provided in Section
1313.99.
(Ord. 2004-115. Passed 8-2-04.)

CHAPTER 1341
General Provisions; Penalty
   EDITOR'S NOTE: This Title Seven contains administrative provisions relevant
to heating and cooling appliances and systems. Reference should also be made to
the BOCA National Mechanical Code (see Section 1301.01(b) herein) and to
Ordinance 62-163, passed December 3, 1962, which is separately published and
not codified herein. Interested persons may obtain copies at cost from the
Building Department. Ordinance 62-163 contains technical provisions for heating
and cooling appliances and systems in one, two and three-family dwellings
(which are not industrialized) and in apartment houses where separate systems
are installed for each dwelling unit.
1341.01   Purpose.

1341.01 PURPOSE.
   In order to provide administrative provisions for the installation of heat
producing devices, air conditioners, ventilating, blower and exhaust systems,
mechanical refrigeration and the installation of gas lines pertinent to such
installations, the following regulations are hereby adopted for the City.
(Ord. 4873. Passed 8-5-57.)
1341.02 SCOPE.
   The provisions of this Title Seven shall govern the sale, location, design,
materials, construction, installation, relocation, alteration, maintenance,
repair and use of any heat-producing device and system, ventilating system,
air-conditioning system, refrigeration, incinerators and boilers in or for one,
two and three-family dwellings within the City. Apartment houses in which
separate heating and/or cooling systems for each dwelling unit are installed
shall be considered single-family dwellings under these regulations.
(Ord. 90-53. Passed 3-5-90.)
1341.03 AUTHORITY OF OTHER DEPARTMENTS.
   Nothing in this Title Seven shall be construed as limiting the authority of
the Fire Division, the Health Department, or other departments of the City, in
making inspections under their respective safety regulations.
(Ord. 4873. Passed 8-5-57.)
1341.04 ELECTRICAL WORK.
   All electrical work in connection with any work covered by this Title Seven
above fifty volts shall be in accordance with the requirements of Chapter
1361 of this Part Thirteen Building Code.
(Ord. 4873. Passed 8-5-57.)
1341.05 OPERATION OF CONDEMNED EQUIPMENT.
   No person shall turn on or permit to be used any equipment covered by this
Title Seven which has been condemned until the cause for condemnation has been
remedied and the equipment or parts thereof have been put in safe condition in
accordance with the requirements of this Title Seven and the office of the
Building Inspector.
(Ord. 4873. Passed 8-5-57.)
1341.06 CONFLICT OF LAWS. (REPEALED)
   (EDITOR'S NOTE: Section
1341.06 was repealed by Ordinance 79-200, passed August 20, 1979.)
1341.99 PENALTY.
   (EDITOR'S NOTE See Section
1313.99 for general Code penalty if no specific penalty is provided.)

1343.01 COMPLIANCE.
   No person, by or through any agent, servant or other party acting on his
behalf, shall install, construct, alter, repair or service any work covered by
this Title Seven without first securing a permit from the Building Inspector.
No owner, occupant, firm, partnership, association, corporation or its agent or
servant shall use any equipment covered by these regulations in any building
which has been installed or altered subsequent to the effective date of this
chapter without a permit as herein provided.
(Ord. 4873. Passed 8-5-57.)
1343.02 HOME OWNER PERMITS.
   No provision of this Title Seven shall be interpreted to require that the
owner of a single-family dwelling shall be franchised or registered or have on
hand a certificate of qualification to personally perform work upon the
premises occupied or to be occupied by the owner thereof as such owner's
established residence. All such work shall be done in conformity with the
provisions of this Title Seven and rules and regulations promulgated thereunder
and no work shall be done unless all permits, inspections and approvals
required by these regulations are secured.
   Whoever misrepresents any material fact in securing a permit under the
provisions of this chapter shall be in violation of this Title Seven and
subject to the penalties provided therefor.
(Ord. 4873. Passed 8-5-57.)
1343.03 APPLICATION.
   Applications for permits to do any work covered by this Title Seven shall be
made on a form provided for such purpose. Such form shall contain sufficient
information for proper description of the work to be performed. Plans,
specifications or additional information shall be supplied when such data is
requested.
(Ord. 4873. Passed 8-5-57.)
1343.04 EXCEPTIONS.
   A permit shall not be required in the case of repairs to any existing system
covered by this Title Seven where the cost of such repairs will not exceed
seventy-five dollars ($75.00) if such repairs do not require dismantling of the
unit and are not of such a nature as to render an inspection necessary in the
opinion of the Building Inspector.
(Ord. 4873. Passed 8-5-57.)
1343.05 MISUSE.
   No franchised contractor shall take out or secure a permit for work to be
done by any person not connected with such firm nor in the employ of such
contractor. No franchised contractor shall allow his name to be used by any
person for the purpose of obtaining a permit. If found guilty, the franchised
contractor shall forfeit his franchise.
(Ord. 4873. Passed 8-5-57.)
1343.06 FEES.
   A fee in accordance with the class of work to be done shall accompany each
application.
   Fees shall be required as set forth in Chapter
109 of the Administrative Code.
(Ord. 2000-238. Passed 11-20-00.)
CHAPTER 1345

1345.01   Insurance requirements.

1345.01 INSURANCE REQUIREMENTS.
   All contractors shall maintain on file a certificate of insurance against
losses arising from any of the work covered by this Title Seven protecting
against injury and death to any person in the amount of fifty thousand dollars
($50,000) for any injury or death to one person and one hundred thousand
dollars ($100,000) for injury or death to all persons and twenty-five thousand
dollars ($25,000) for damage to property and shall, further, furnish evidence
of the same to the Building Inspector. However, any corporation having net
assets in the amount of five million dollars ($5,000,000) over and above all
liabilities need not comply with the provisions of this section if its officers
furnish, at the time of application for a franchise, a financial statement,
renewable yearly, and an indemnification letter holding the City harmless
against all claims of public liability and property damage.
(Ord. 4873. Passed 8-5-57.)
1345.02 PERFORMANCE BOND REQUIREMENTS.
   All franchised contractors shall furnish and maintain on file at the office
of the Building Inspector a performance bond of one thousand five hundred
dollars ($1,500) which shall cover construction, installation, repair and
alteration required by this Title Seven.
(Ord. 4873. Passed 8-5-57.)
1345.03 BOND PROVISIONS.
   The bonding company shall employ a franchised contractor to complete or make
corrections when the bonded contractor fails to perform such work in accordance
with this Title Seven when ordered to do so by the Board of Building Standards
and Appeals.
(Ord. 4873. Passed 8-5-57.)
1345.04 JOINT INSURANCE AND BOND REQUIREMENTS.
   When a firm, corporation or association furnishes the certificate of
insurance and bond, such certificate and bond shall also include the name of
the person who is approved by the Board of Building Standards and Appeals for
franchising.
(Ord. 4873. Passed 8-5-57.)

1347.01 DUTIES OF BUILDING INSPECTOR.
   It shall be the duty of the Building Inspector and his deputy inspectors to
enforce or cause to be enforced the provisions of this Title Seven.
(Ord. 4873. Passed 8-5-57.)
1347.02 SUPERVISION OF TESTS.
   The Building Inspector shall supervise all tests necessary to meet the
requirements of this Title Seven as required by Section
1347.06.
(Ord. 4873. Passed 8-5-57.)
1347.03 APPLICATION FOR PERMITS.
   The Building Inspector shall approve or disapprove applications for permits
covering requirements of this Title Seven.
(Ord. 4873. Passed 8-5-57.)
1347.04 PLANS AND SPECIFICATIONS.
   The Building Inspector may require plans, specifications and any additional
information deemed necessary before approving permit applications for
installations or alterations.
(Ord. 4873. Passed 8-5-57.)
1347.05 APPROVAL OF BOARD OF BUILDING STANDARDS AND APPEALS.
   The Building Inspector shall submit to the Board of Building Standards and
Appeals for the approval or disapproval by such Board any materials or devices
not specifically provided for in these regulations.
(Ord. 4873. Passed 8-5-57.)
1347.06 TESTS OF INSTALLATION OF PRODUCTS.
   The Building Inspector may require such tests deemed necessary to properly
ascertain the safety of a product or installation covered by these regulations.
(Ord. 4873. Passed 8-5-57.)
1347.07 CONCEALED WORK.
   The Building Inspector may require the immediate removal of any material or
construction found to have been so installed as to conceal or cover up any
newly installed portion of an installation or system before an opportunity is
given for inspection and approval.
(Ord. 4873. Passed 8-5-57.)
1347.08 INSPECTION TAGS.
   Upon completion and final inspection of any installation, alteration or
repair covered by a permit, the Building Inspector shall place an approval or
disapproval label or tag on such work.
(Ord. 4873. Passed 8-5-57.)
1347.09 FRANCHISE APPLICATIONS.
   The Building Inspector shall accept applications for franchises and shall
supervise the written examination. He shall submit such examination and results
to the Board of Building Standards and Appeals for final approval or
disapproval.
(Ord. 4873. Passed 8-5-57.)
1347.10 MODIFICATION OF CODE.
   The Building Inspector shall submit recommendations to the Board of Building
Standards and Appeals on Heating and Cooling Code changes, alterations or
additions.
(Ord. 4873. Passed 8-5-57.)
1347.11 RIGHT OF ENTRY.
   The Building Inspector and his authorized assistants shall have the right,
during reasonable hours, to enter any building or premises, within the
jurisdiction of this Title Seven, for the purpose of making any inspections or
tests of any equipment or parts thereof covered by this Title Seven.
(Ord. 4873. Passed 8-5-57.)
1347.12 INSPECTION OF HAZARDS.
   It shall be the duty of the Building Inspector to inspect any equipment
covered by these regulations which, due to its construction, installation or
condition, may present a hazard to persons or property.
(Ord. 4873. Passed 8-5-57.)
1347.13 RIGHT TO CONDEMN.
   The Building Inspector shall condemn and order discontinuance of the use of
any equipment or installation covered by these regulations which constitutes a
hazard to life, health or property.
(Ord. 4873. Passed 8-5-57.)
1347.14 FINAL INSPECTION.
   The Building Inspector shall make final inspection of completed
installations within fifteen days of receipt of a completion notice, or prior
to occupancy.
(Ord. 4873. Passed 8-5-57.)

1361.01 ADOPTION OF NATIONAL ELECTRICAL CODE BY REFERENCE.
   Pursuant to Section
4.14 of the City Charter, there is hereby adopted, for the purpose of
prescribing regulations governing conditions hazardous to life and property,
the National Electrical Code, being the edition referenced in the current
edition of the Ohio Building Code, as amended and adopted by the Ohio Board of
Building Standards, Department of Commerce. Such Code is hereby adopted and
incorporated as if fully set out at length herein, except as hereinafter
amended, and from the date on which this section takes effect, the provisions
thereof shall be controlling in the City.
(Ord. 2004-116. Passed 8-2-04.)
1361.02 FILE AND DISTRIBUTION COPIES.
   One copy of the National Electrical Code, as adopted in Section
1361.01, is on file with the Clerk of Council for inspection by the public.
(Ord. 97-38. Passed 2-3-97; Ord. 2004-116. Passed 8-2-04.)
1361.03 OBJECT AND PURPOSE.
   The object and purpose of this chapter is to safeguard persons and property
from hazards arising from the use of electrical energy by establishing and
adopting minimum standards for the installation and maintenance of electrical
systems, the issuance of permits, the collection of fees, the inspection and
approval of material, equipment and installations and the administration and
enforcement of the provisions and regulations contained herein.
(Ord. 97-38. Passed 2-3-97; Ord. 2004-116. Passed 8-2-04.)
1361.04 SCOPE.
   This chapter and the regulations included herein shall cover electrical
conductors, apparatus and equipment and the installation, alteration or repair
of the same, for purposes of supplying and utilizing electricity for light,
heat, power, signal and controls, within or on public and private buildings and
other structures and premises within the City, including yards, carnival lots,
sales lots, parking lots, trailer or mobile home parks, recreation and
electrical signs and displays, and the conductors that connect the
installations to a supply of electricity, as well as other outside conductors
on or adjacent to the premises.
(Ord. 97-38. Passed 2-3-97; Ord. 2004-116. Passed 8-2-04.)
1361.05 REGISTRATION REQUIRED; EXCEPTIONS.
   No person, firm or corporation shall install, maintain, alter or repair, or
engage in the business of installing, maintaining, altering or repairing,
within the City, any electrical wiring, devices, apparatus or equipment unless
such person, firm or corporation has received from the City, in accordance with
the regulations herein provided, an electrical contractor's registration and
certificate for the same, unless such person is employed by and working under
the direction of a holder of an Elyria City electrical registration. However,
the electrical registration regulations of this chapter shall not apply to the
following:
   (a)   The installation, alteration or repair of electrical generation,
transmission or distribution equipment, and the utilization of equipment owned
and operated by an electrical public utility company or the City;
   (b)   The installation, alteration or repair of signal or communication
equipment, where such equipment is owned and operated by a public utility
company or the City;
   (c)   Any work on ships, railway cars, trackless trolleys, buses, aircraft
and automobiles;
   (d)   Any work in connection with electrical equipment used for radio and
television transmission and reception, but not including supply wires to such
equipment;
   (e)   Any work involved in the manufacturing or testing of electrical
equipment or apparatus, but not including any permanent wiring or equipment;
   (f)   Any work associated with:
      (1)   The repair of plug-connected electrical appliances or devices; or
      (2)   Permanently connected electrical appliances or devices which have
been electrically and mechanically disconnected and separated from all sources
of electrical supply by a registered electrical contractor. The opening of
switches or the blowing or removal of fuses shall not be considered as
electrical or mechanical disconnection or separation.
   (g)   The installation or replacement of approved fuses which are not
oversized for the circuit involved;
   (h)   The installation or replacement of approved pin-type lamps, screw-base
lamps or plug- connected portable appliances which do not overload the circuit
involved and are not located in hazardous locations.
   Other exceptions from the provisions of this chapter are as set forth in
Section
1321.07.
(Ord. 97-38. Passed 2-3-97; Ord. 2004-116. Passed 8-2-04.)
1361.06 APPLICATION FOR REGISTRATION.
   An application for registration shall be made in writing to the Building
Department, stating the name, address and place of business of the principal of
the firm or corporation making the application who will act as the supervisor
of the work to be performed under the registration. All applications for
registration shall be reviewed by the Electrical Inspector and the Building
Inspector.
(Ord. 97-38. Passed 2-3-97; Ord. 2004-116. Passed 8-2-04.)
1361.07 REGISTRATION HOLDER.
   Each applicant for a registration issued in accordance with the provisions
of this chapter shall have obtained a state license which was issued pursuant
to Ohio R.C. Chapter 4740. In the event any registered holder is associated
with or employed by a business and such association with or the employment of
the holder of a City registration is terminated, such business shall notify the
Building Official within ten days of such termination and such registration
shall become void after 90 days unless another associate or employee of said
business, licensed by the State of Ohio, becomes registered. No registration or
certificate issued in accordance with the provisions of this chapter shall be
assignable or transferable.
(Ord. 97-38. Passed 2-3-97; Ord. 2004-116. Passed 8-2-04.)
1361.08 REVOCATION OF REGISTRATION.
   Any registered electrical contractor's registration may be suspended or
revoked by the Building Inspector in accordance with Section
1321.05.
(Ord. 97-38. Passed 2-3-97; Ord. 2004-116. Passed 8-2-04.)
1361.09 WIRING, DEVICES, ETC.; PERMIT REQUIRED.
   No person, firm or corporation shall maintain, alter or repair any
electrical wiring, devices, appliances or equipment unless such person, firm or
corporation first obtains a permit from the Building Department, or unless such
person, firm or corporation, or the work involved, is specifically exempted by
this chapter.
(Ord. 97-38. Passed 2-3-97; Ord. 2004-116. Passed 8-2-04.)
1361.10 PERMIT APPLICATION.
   An application for a permit shall be filed in writing with the Building
Department on a form furnished for that purpose and signed by the applicant.
The application shall give the correct address of the work and describe and
enumerate the work, with such other information as may be required.
(Ord. 97-38. Passed 2-3-97; Ord. 2004-116. Passed 8-2-04.)
1361.11 DRAWINGS AND SPECIFICATIONS REQUIRED.
   Drawings and specifications shall be required, in sufficient detail, to
enable the Electrical Inspector to determine that any proposed work for which a
permit has been applied for will be in conformity with the provisions of this
chapter.
(Ord. 97-38. Passed 2-3-97; Ord. 2004-116. Passed 8-2-04.)
1361.12 PERMIT FEES.
   Fees for electrical permits shall be as provided in Section
109.13 of the Administrative Code.
(Ord. 97-38. Passed 2-3-97; Ord. 2004-116. Passed 8-2-04.)
1361.13 APPROVAL OF MATERIALS, DEVICES, ETC.
   All electrical materials, devices, fixtures, appliances, illuminated signs
and other equipment used or installed in the City shall be of a type approved
by the Board of Building Standards. Unless specifically disapproved by formal
action of the Board, electrical materials, devices, fixtures, appliances,
illuminated signs and other equipment that bear the label of approval of
Underwriters' Laboratories, Inc., or any other agency approved by the State
Board of Building Standards, shall be deemed approved by the Board.
(Ord. 97-38. Passed 2-3-97; Ord. 2004-116. Passed 8-2-04.)
1361.14 INSPECTIONS, TESTS AND APPROVALS.
   (a)   All electrical wiring and equipment installed, altered, replaced or
repaired in or about any building, structure or premises with the City of
Elyria shall be subject to inspection and approval by the Electrical Inspector.
   (b)   No electrical wiring or parts thereof shall be covered or concealed
until the Electrical Inspector has approved the installation and given
permission to cover or conceal the same. It shall be the duty of the person
obtaining the permit to give 24 hours notice to the Electrical Inspector when
work is ready for inspection. Work shall be inspected as soon as possible after
receipt of such notice and, when found to conform to the provisions of this
chapter, an official notice of approval shall be posted in a conspicuous place
by the Electrical Inspector.
(Ord. 97-38. Passed 2-3-97; Ord. 2004-116. Passed 8-2-04.)
1361.15 FINAL INSPECTION AND APPROVAL.
   (a)   All work covered by this chapter shall be submitted for final
inspection and approval before being placed in service.
   (b)   Tests necessary to verify that an installation is in conformity with
the requirements of this chapter shall be performed in the presence of the
Electrical Inspector and any equipment, material, power and labor necessary for
such tests shall be furnished by the holder of the permit.
   (c)   When an inspection shows that work submitted for inspection is
incomplete or not in conformity with the requirements of this chapter, the
permit holder shall make the necessary corrections or additions and request a
re-inspection.
(Ord. 97-38. Passed 2-3-97; Ord. 2004-116. Passed 8-2-04.)
1361.16 LIABILITY.
   This chapter shall not be construed as imposing on the City any liability or
responsibility for damages resulting from any defective electrical work or
equipment or the installation thereof, nor shall the City or any official or
employee thereof be held to assume any liability or responsibility by reason of
any act or action taken in enforcing the provisions of this chapter or carrying
out the duties authorized and required by this chapter. Any lawsuit or action
brought against any City official, employee or board member by reason of any
action, or an action committed in the discharge of his or her duties under this
chapter, shall be defended by the City Solicitor until the final termination of
proceedings in such action.
(Ord. 97-38. Passed 2-3-97; Ord. 2004-116. Passed 8-2-04.)
1361.17 INSTALLATION STANDARDS.
   All installations of electrical wiring and equipment for lighting, heating,
signal or power shall be made in strict accordance with the provisions of this
chapter and any orders, rules and regulations issued by authority thereof.
Where no specific standards are prescribed by this chapter or by any orders or
statutes of the State, the regulations of the Ohio Building Code for the safety
of persons and property shall be required under this chapter.
(Ord. 97-38. Passed 2-3-97; Ord. 2004-116. Passed 8-2-04.)
1361.18 UNDERGROUND ELECTRICAL AND COMMUNICATION WIRING.
   Within the boundary of all urban renewal projects, all new residential
subdivisions and all new manufactured home parks, any new electrical
distribution wiring, any new communication wiring and any new street lighting
wiring, shall be constructed underground.
(Ord. 97-38. Passed 2-3-97; Ord. 2004-116. Passed 8-2-04.)
1361.19 SERVICE AND METERING; DISCONNECTING MEANS.
   (a)   Service and metering shall be in accordance with the National
Electrical Code, except as modified herein.
   (b)   Every electrical contractor shall leave his or her name, address and
telephone number on the main electrical panel to enable the Electrical
Inspector to communicate promptly with the contractor when necessary.
(Ord. 97-38. Passed 2-3-97; Ord. 2004-116. Passed 8-2-04.)
1361.99 PENALTY
   The penalty for any violation of the provisions of Chapter
1361 shall be as provided in Section
1313.99.
(Ord. 2004-116. Passed 8-2-04.)

1385.01 FIRE LIMITS - "AREA A."
   (a)   The area included within the following boundaries shall be known as
Fire Limits Area A": The "B-2" Business District as shown on the present
official Zoning Map of the City and as may he amended and extended hereafter.
   (b)   Only type I A-B and II A-B construction, as defined in the Ohio
Building Code as adopted in Chapter
1301 shall be permitted in Fire Limits "Area A" for all new construction and
for all additions, alterations, remodeling or repair which necessitate that
more than fifty percent of the building will require such work to be done. A
temporary builder's construction building may be of Type V construction and
shall be removed upon completion of construction work.
(Ord. 4919. Passed 1-20-58.)
1385.02 FIRE LIMITS - "AREA B."
   (a)   The following areas shall be designated as Fire Limits "Area B": The
"B-1" Neighborhood Business and "B-3" General Business Districts as shown on
the present official Zoning Map and as may be amended to extend such districts
or other areas that may be rezoned into these classifications.
   (b)   Classification of construction within Industrial Areas ("M-1" Light,
"M-2" Heavy) shall be in accordance with the Ohio Building Code, as adopted in
Chapter
1301, concerning proposed use and exposure, except that Type V construction is
prohibited unless such construction is in compliance with subsection (c)
hereof.
   (c)   No new construction, or any remodeling, alterations, additions or
repairs affecting more than fifty percent of the building on which work is to
be done, shall be less than Type IV construction, except that accessory
buildings that are distant at least twenty feet from any other building on the
same lot and distant at least twenty feet from every lot line and consisting of
not more than 500 square feet in total area, may be of Type V construction or
may be a metal building. No flammable, explosive or any other material that may
create hazardous conditions shall be stored in a Type V building or in a metal
building. A temporary builder's construction building may be of Type V
construction and shall be removed when construction work is completed.
(Ord. 4919. Passed 1-20-58.)
1385.03 MOVING BUILDING INTO FIRE LIMITS.
   No building shall be moved to a location inside the fire limits unless such
building is of the type of construction permitted in such fire limits, except
that a temporary builder's construction building may be of Type V construction,
shall be used exclusively by such builder and shall be removed when
construction work is completed.
(Ord. 4919. Passed 1-20-58.)
1385.04 ENFORCEMENT.
   This chapter shall be enforced according to the requirements and penalties
set forth in this Part Thirteen - Building Code.
(Ord. 4919. Passed 1-20-58.)
